# Russet (03, architect) — SPD-065

## Brief
Revise the Phase 1 spike docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md in place to a real-module package design for bin/spud_ledger.py. Planning and prototyping only: nothing under bin/ or tests/ changes in the repository. Burbank's one-namespace version is committed at 6d412b4 and stays in git history; reuse its responsibility map, move list, test-attribute survey, hook self-recognition table, timing harness and verification recipe wherever they still hold, and re-check anything you rely on.

Eric's decisions on Burbank's spike (2026-09-15):
1. **Real modules, not one namespace.** A package whose modules import what they use. The design where the entry executes part files into its own namespace is declined.
2. **A hook run imports only what the hooks need.** Render, import, the command modules the hooks do not call, project install, schedule, doctor and the parser stay out of the hook path's imports.
3. **Modules over ~250 lines stay whole** when they are one cohesive class, function or job. ~250 is the look-again point, never a cap.
4. **Phase 2 extras, all approved:** a guard test; the timing harness committed as tests/probes/hook_timing.py; the one copy line in tests/probes/headless.py fixed (that closes SPD-052).

What the revision must settle, each with evidence from a prototype built in scratch copies, never in the repository:

a. **Import style and cycles.** Burbank found one strongly connected group of 10 shell parts, render/cost with render/teamcard, state/backup with state/db, and 27 references to a later part (spike §2.4). Propose how each is resolved: regrouping so the graph is acyclic; `from . import module` with attribute access at call time (`walk.ShellWalk(...)`), which tolerates a cycle at import time and keeps a patch on the defining module landing; a function-local import; or moving shared constants down a layer. List every code edit the resolution needs. A mechanical call-site rewrite from `name` to `module.name` is acceptable when listed; a behaviour change is not. Show the final import graph and prove no import-time cycle can fail, or give the reason each remaining cycle is safe.
b. **Where a name is patched.** Today `mock.patch.object(spud, "do_backup")` and `backup_stamp` in tests/test_backup.py (228, 264, 303) land because every call site resolves in one namespace. Evaluate at least two answers with a prototype run: (i) the tests patch the defining module, with the exact edits listed; (ii) the entry module is a module subclass (`sys.modules[__name__].__class__ = ...`) whose reads fall through to the defining module and whose `__setattr__` forwards there, so the suite and the public surface are untouched. Recommend one.
c. **The public API is unchanged**, per Eric's Phase 1 requirement: every attribute the launcher and the suite read on `spud_ledger` (Burbank's §4.2 list, plus `main` and `__file__`) stays reachable as `spud_ledger.<name>` from the original entry point. Say how the entry re-exports without importing the command-only modules on a hook run (decision 2).
d. **Module-global state.** `LazyModule.__getattr__` rebinds the name in the globals of the module defining the class (around line 43); `git_own_commands` rebinds `_GIT_OWN_COMMANDS` with `global`; `_WORKTREES`, `ACTIVE_CTX` (around 1204) and any other module-level name that is rebound or mutated. For each: which module owns it, and how every reader sees the same value.
e. **Loader and bytecode under `python3.14 -I -S`.** How bin/spud makes the package importable without the working directory and without putting a directory on sys.path where a module name could shadow the standard library (a meta-path finder that answers only the package's own name from the directory beside the launcher's real path is one option; measure what it costs). Every module's bytecode is cached under the home's state-directory pycache, mirroring its source path, so a worktree's program and the main checkout's never share a file. Nothing is written when that directory is absent, and no `__pycache__` ever appears under bin/. Name the package directory and say why (`spud_ledger.d` is not importable, and a `bin/spud_ledger/` package beside `bin/spud_ledger.py` collides on the name).
f. **Hook latency.** Measure with the harness of spike §5.3, main against the prototype, import-system overhead included. The pass is each hook median within 1 ms of main's in the same run; if the design cannot meet it, say by how much and what would.
g. **The guard test** for this design: no import-time cycle; the hook path's transitive imports exclude the command-only modules; every module in the package is reachable from the entry. Say where it lives and what it parses.
h. **Behaviour evidence.** A prototype built mechanically from the move list plus the listed edits, run through the suite in a scratch copy against a control of today's program (as in spike §6.3), and through the CLI and hook smoke script.

Keep the spike's nine sections, updated: 1 responsibility map; 2 tree, loader, and the cycle resolution in place of Burbank's §2.4; 3 move list with every top-level name in exactly one module, checked by script; 4 compatibility (entry point, suite with its exact edits, hook self-recognition); 5 hook latency; 6 Phase 2 commits in Eric's order (shared types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components, then the entry as orchestrator), each leaving the suite green, with the extras placed; 7 modules over ~250 and why each stays whole; 8 CLAUDE.md lines that change; 9 open questions, each with a recommendation. Rewrite the recommendation summary at the top and say plainly what changed from Burbank's version. Anchor line numbers to the file on main now (`git log -1 --format=%h -- bin/spud_ledger.py`); if it moved since 9e1deda, re-anchor.
